analysis:
This PR is documentation-only: docs/developer/test.md gains a 'Provider authorization guidance' section (patch hunk head lines 76-87) and docs/provider/attestation.md gains a paragraph at head line 141-142 plus a date bump. The supplied text units for test.md (head lines 1843-2547) are unchanged surrounding documentation, with no code, secrets, or policy changes. Examined against TB-011, T-053, T-054, T-057 and T-058, and against T-041 for the cache-related test prose.

The new attestation.md guidance tells operators to keep MDM profiles installed and wait for a fresh coordinator decision when App Attest authorizes serving but MDM-removal readiness is stale. This is conservative. It states that the serving lease can stay valid after removal readiness goes stale, and that a 10-second decision freshness, a current daemon snapshot and unexpired authorization are required. It also says a local state-file rewrite cannot extend readiness. That matches the threat model's position that the coordinator, not local state, is authoritative, and it does not claim to widen authorization. It does not weaken T-053 (stale authorization) or T-057 (premature MDM removal). If anything it reduces the risk of premature profile removal.

The test.md addition describes ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests as using fixed snapshots and injected process identity, and disclaims native App Attest acceptance. It makes no overclaim (T-056).

Remaining unverified: the described behavior in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Diagnostics/ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift and its tests is outside the supplied evidence, so the docs' accuracy against code is unconfirmed. The attestation.md patch excerpt is truncated after the unenroll paragraph; the visible content is unchanged context. No findings.
